title: Two UN bodies elect the same international judges
body: The International Court of Justice has 15 judges with nine-year terms. Candidates need an absolute majority in both the UN General Assembly and the Security Council, which vote separately.
takeaway: A candidate winning in one chamber still needs enough support in the other to take a seat.
source: United Nations, Statute of the International Court of Justice, Articles 3 to 13

title: Australia's two houses met in 1974 to vote together on six bills
body: A double dissolution ends the terms of both Australian houses and sends all seats to an election. If the same legislative deadlock continues afterwards, a joint sitting may follow. In August 1974 such a sitting considered six bills.
takeaway: The procedure offers a way to resolve certain disagreements after voters have elected both houses again.
source: Parliament of Australia, Senate Brief 8, The Senate and Legislation
